source_refs.note: Topic 1.15 (PDF 20-21). The book has no figure here; the backup-types figure is original. The incremental definition is made precise and the restore example is added.

blocks.text: Data backup means making a copy of important data to protect it from loss or damage, for example by a virus or a hardware failure. A backup lets data be restored easily; recovery is the process of getting the data back. Every user should back up data regularly.

blocks.caption: Types of data backup
rows: Only the data changed since the last backup of any kind
All the changes since the last full backup

blocks.text: Backups can be stored on hard drives or in cloud storage.

blocks.alt: A grid with days Sunday to Wednesday across the top. Row full every day: an 'all data' box each day. Row incremental: 'all data' on Sunday, then small equal boxes 'Mon only', 'Tue only', 'Wed only'. Row differential: 'all data' on Sunday, then 'since Sun' boxes that grow wider each day. A note: incremental is smallest and fastest but restoring needs the full backup and every later piece; differential grows each day but restoring needs only the full backup and the latest differential.
blocks.caption: Full, incremental and differential backups over four days (original diagram).
blocks.long_description: The choice is a trade-off between the time and space each backup takes and how many pieces are needed to restore the data.

items: Backup files are used to restore lost data.
Recovery software helps get deleted files back.
System restore can recover system data.
Professionals can recover data from damaged devices.

blocks.prompt: A full backup is taken on Sunday and incremental backups on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. The disk fails on Thursday. Which backups are needed to restore the data?
blocks.explanation: Sunday's full backup and all three incremental backups (Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday), applied in order. With differential backups, only Sunday's full backup and Wednesday's differential would be needed.

items: Backup: a copy of important data; recovery: getting it back.
Full: everything; incremental: changes since the last backup; differential: changes since the last full backup.
Recovery: backup files, recovery software, system restore, professionals.
